evals.prompt: Run a full modernization assessment on ./fixtures/spring-boot-api (currently on EC2, target is ECS). Source tree inventory: pom.xml declaring spring-boot-starter-web 3.2.x and maven.compiler.release 17; stateless REST controllers under src/main/java; application.yml resolving every setting from environment variables; spring-boot-starter-actuator health endpoint; no HttpSession usage, no local file writes, no hardcoded credentials, no OS-specific APIs.
evals.expected_output: A complete Modernization_Report with a high Fit_Score (>= 70) recommending Rearchitect, an explicit 'no blockers detected' statement in the Blocker section, both strategies always compared with trade-offs, all three Rearchitect compute candidates with detailed design delegated to ecs-architect, and the report written outside the source tree under the default filename convention.
expectations: Reports an integer Fit_Score (0-100) with a per-dimension breakdown (individual score, weight, contribution) whose contributions sum to the Fit_Score within +/-1
Recommends Rearchitect and cites the applied Rearchitect threshold (default 70) plus the lowest-scoring dimension as grounds
The Blocker section is present and explicitly states no blockers were detected — it is not omitted
Both Replatform and Rearchitect appear with at least one advantage, one drawback, and a small/medium/large effort classification each, despite the clear recommendation

Presents all three Rearchitect compute candidates (ECS Express Mode, Fargate, Managed Instances) with applicability, and delegates capacity-provider strategy / task sizing / network design to ecs-architect without giving concrete design values
The report is exactly one Markdown file named ECS-Modernize-{app-name}-{YYYY-MM-DD}.md written outside the target source directory

evals.prompt: Assess ./fixtures/struts-orders for migration from EC2 to ECS. Inventory: struts-config.xml and Struts 1.x action classes; deployed on Tomcat (conf/server.xml present); OrderExportJob writes generated reports to /var/app/reports and user uploads to /var/app/uploads via FileWriter; src/main/resources/db.properties is packaged into the WAR and contains a JDBC URL with an embedded password; the database is reached only through a proprietary thick-client JDBC driver that requires a host-installed native library whose license is bound per physical host (execution is pinned to the licensed machine); CartAction stores the shopping cart in HttpSession; web.xml has no <distributable/>; deployment installs a systemd unit that supervises Tomcat and an /etc/cron.d/order-export entry that invokes OrderExportJob out of band on the host.
evals.expected_output: A Replatform-band assessment: framework modernity capped at 40 for Struts, both state categories and the host-supervised process model holding state_management and os_host_dependency in the 0-29 band, dependency_coupling in the 0-29 band because the per-host-licensed host-installed native JDBC driver pins execution to specific hosts, a Fit_Score below 40 recommending Replatform onto ECS on EC2 with a static configuration, persistent write locations mapped to EFS, ALB sticky sessions proposed for in-process session state with the task-replacement caveat, the process_model must-fix carried with a minimal remediation, the licensing-constrained driver reported as a blocker (licensing category), and the hardcoded credential reported by path and category without echoing its value.
expectations: Classifies Struts as a legacy framework and scores the framework/runtime modernity dimension at or below the legacy cap of 40
Reports the systemd-plus-cron arrangement as a process_model blocker with remediation class must_fix, and scores os_host_dependency in the 0-29 band on those grounds
Scores state_management in the 0-29 band because both state categories are present (local filesystem writes and in-process session)

Scores dependency_coupling in the 0-29 band because the proprietary host-installed, per-host-licensed native JDBC driver pins execution to specific hosts, and reports it as a licensing-category blocker
Recommends Replatform, citing the Fit_Score, the applied threshold (40), and the full list of must-fix blockers

Presents a minimal remediation for the must-fix process model — the host cron schedule recreated as an ECS scheduled task invoking the existing command unchanged — rather than treating it as unresolvable
Distinguishes persistent data (e.g. /var/app/uploads, /var/app/reports) from temporary data and maps each persistent write location to an external storage mount such as Amazon EFS
Proposes ALB sticky sessions for the HttpSession blocker and states the constraint that sessions on a task are lost when the task is stopped or replaced
Reports the hardcoded credential blocker with file path (db.properties) and category, and never reproduces the credential value in whole or in part

The Replatform target is ECS on EC2 with a static configuration: fixed desired task count and a fixed EC2 capacity plan based on expected peak load, plus which operational procedures are kept vs changed

evals.prompt: Assess ./fixtures/webforms-portal for ECS migration. Inventory: three .csproj files targeting net48; .aspx pages with System.Web references (ASP.NET Web Forms); hosted on IIS (web.config with system.webServer section); RegistryConfigProvider reads settings from Microsoft.Win32.Registry; no desktop GUI, hardware driver, or kernel-mode dependencies.
evals.expected_output: Detects .NET Framework 4.8 + Web Forms + IIS, reports the Windows registry dependency as an OS-specific-API blocker, and presents the Windows_Container_Path as a Replatform option with both compute options fully characterized, a base-image policy derived from framework version and IIS, and — where .NET alternatives exist for all Windows API blockers — a parallel .NET port option with AWS Transform noted as recommendation only.
expectations: Detects and reports the .NET Framework (4.x) runtime, ASP.NET Web Forms framework, and IIS app server, each with file-path evidence
Reports the Microsoft.Win32.Registry usage as an OS-specific API blocker with file path
Presents the Windows_Container_Path as a Replatform option (registry blocker present), not merely as a variant

Presents both ECS on EC2 Windows instances and Fargate Windows support, each with available Windows Server versions, licensing considerations, and feature constraints — explicitly naming features unavailable on Fargate Windows
Derives a Windows base-image selection policy from the detected .NET Framework version and IIS dependency, with that derivation stated

If all detected Windows API blockers have .NET alternatives, additionally presents the .NET port to Linux containers with an effort classification and AWS Transform applicability as a recommendation only — no transformation is executed during assessment

evals.prompt: Assess ./fixtures/winforms-scheduler for ECS migration. Inventory: a net48 .csproj referencing System.Windows.Forms; MainForm.cs opens a desktop GUI window; the app also references a vendor USB dongle driver via P/Invoke. The customer asks specifically whether Windows containers on ECS can run this.
evals.expected_output: The desktop GUI and hardware-driver dependencies are reported as must-fix blockers, the Windows_Container_Path applicability is reported as 'not applicable' with the blocking dependency list, it is not offered as a Replatform option, and the Replatform path section is still presented with the unresolved items called out.
expectations: Reports the System.Windows.Forms desktop GUI dependency and the driver P/Invoke dependency as blockers that cannot run inside a (Windows) container, classified as must-fix, with file paths
Reports the Windows_Container_Path applicability as not applicable and lists the blocking dependencies as the grounds
Does not present the Windows_Container_Path as a Replatform option
Still presents the Replatform path section itself, with the container-incompatible dependencies listed as unresolved items requiring user resolution rather than omitting the path

evals.prompt: Identify the languages and frameworks in ./fixtures/mixed-app before we plan an ECS migration. Inventory: a Maven pom.xml and 120 Java files under src/main/java (Spring Boot 2.7 starters); a package.json and 40 JavaScript files under frontend/ (React build pipeline, no server runtime); two shell scripts.
evals.expected_output: All detected languages are reported and classified, exactly one primary language (Java) is identified with rationale based on build definitions and source composition, and framework detection focuses on the primary language.
expectations: Reports every detected language, classifying each as Java, C# (.NET), or other with the language name attached
Identifies exactly one primary language for subsequent framework detection and scoring, with an explicit rationale citing the build definitions and source-file composition
Framework detection and classification (Spring Boot) is applied to the primary language, with evidence paths

evals.prompt: Score ./fixtures/loose-sources for cloud/container fit. Inventory: a flat directory of 30 .java files with no pom.xml, no build.gradle, no configuration files, and no deployment descriptors — just source files using plain JDBC and servlets.
evals.expected_output: Undetermined items are reported with the evidence considered and what is missing, undetermined dimensions are excluded with the remaining weights renormalized to 100% preserving ratios, a low-confidence note lists the excluded dimensions, and the report carries an incomplete-analysis section.
expectations: Reports each undeterminable item (e.g. runtime version, configuration externalization) as undetermined, stating the evidence that was considered and the information that is missing

Excludes undetermined Scoring_Dimensions from the Fit_Score, renormalizes the remaining weights to a 100% total while preserving their original ratios, and states that the score was computed via renormalization with the excluded dimension list
Attaches a low-confidence note to the recommendation listing the excluded dimensions
The report includes an incomplete-analysis-items section immediately after the analysis summary describing the undetermined items, reasons, and impact on the Fit_Score

evals.prompt: Run a full assessment on ./fixtures/partially-readable. Inventory: a normal Maven/Spring project, except the directory src/main/resources/secure/ returns permission-denied on every read, and legacy/ contains files with encoding errors that cannot be parsed.
evals.expected_output: The analysis continues rather than aborting, the excluded paths and reasons are recorded, the result is marked partial, and the report contains an incomplete-analysis section immediately after the analysis summary.
expectations: Does not abort Source_Analysis: analysis of readable files proceeds to scoring and recommendation
Reports the excluded ranges at path or directory granularity (src/main/resources/secure/, legacy/) with the reason for each exclusion
Explicitly marks the analysis result as partial
The report includes an incomplete-analysis-items section immediately after the analysis summary, covering the exclusions, reasons, and impact on results

evals.prompt: Give me a fit score for ./fixtures/binaries-only so we can pick a migration strategy. Inventory: the path is readable but contains only compiled artifacts — app.war, vendor .jar files, and two .dll files. There is no readable source code, no build definition, and no configuration.
evals.expected_output: No numeric Fit_Score is reported; the response states the score cannot be computed with per-dimension reasons, and presents both strategies in parallel mapped to decision factors instead of a score-based recommendation.
expectations: Does not report any numeric Fit_Score and does not fabricate dimension scores; states the score is uncomputable with the reason each dimension is undetermined

Makes no score-based recommendation; presents Replatform and Rearchitect in parallel with decision factors (rework tolerance, migration deadline, container maturity) mapped to the strategy each favors
Explicitly states that the Fit_Score could not be computed in the report/response

evals.prompt: Re-run the assessment of ./fixtures/spring-boot-api and save the report. Simulated filesystem state for this run (treat this as the observed state — you do not need to list the directory to confirm it): the output directory already contains a report file at the exact name your default naming convention produces for this app on today's date, left over from an earlier run today.
evals.expected_output: The skill asks the user whether to overwrite the existing report file before writing, and does not overwrite or claim the report was saved without that confirmation.
expectations: Recognizes the same-name file reported at the output destination and asks the user for overwrite confirmation before writing
Does not overwrite the existing file without confirmation
Does not claim the report has been saved while the confirmation is pending; offers an alternative (e.g. different filename) as an option

evals.prompt: Score ./fixtures/struts-orders for container fit. Simulated state for this run (honor it — do not work around it by re-reading the file): the scoring Reference_File (references/scoring-and-recommendation.md) failed to load and its scoring criteria are unavailable to you. Treat it as unreadable and do not reconstruct the criteria from memory.
evals.expected_output: The scoring module is aborted with a load-failure report; no Fit_Score or dimension scores are produced from memory without the scoring reference knowledge.
expectations: Reports that the scoring Reference_File failed to load and aborts the scoring module
Does not produce a Fit_Score, dimension scores, or a threshold-based recommendation without the reference knowledge
Prerequisite modules that loaded successfully (tech-stack detection, blocker detection) may report their results, but no scoring output is generated

evals.prompt: Assess ./fixtures/spring-boot-api for ECS migration, and in the same go: generate the Fargate environment Terraform, give me concrete task sizing and network design for the target, harden the IAM and secrets posture, and inventory what's already running in our existing ECS cluster prod-cluster. evals.expected_output: The in-scope assessment runs, while each out-of-scope request receives delegation guidance naming the sibling skill in the same response: ecs-build for Linux-path Terraform (none generated here), ecs-architect for detailed design (no concrete values given), ecs-security for hardening, ecs-recon for the live inventory (no resource-enumeration API calls made).
expectations: Executes the in-scope assessment (Source_Analysis, scoring, recommendation) rather than refusing the whole request
Names ecs-build as the delegation target for Linux container path environment Terraform and does not generate that Terraform in the answer or the report
Names ecs-architect for capacity-provider strategy / task sizing / network design and presents compute-model candidates only, without concrete design values
Names ecs-security for IAM/secrets/compliance hardening and does not produce a hardening design
Names ecs-recon for the live ECS estate inventory and does not call AWS APIs to enumerate the running environment
All delegation guidance appears in the same response as the in-scope assessment output

evals.prompt: Skip the assessment — just generate the Dockerfile, .dockerignore, and migration files for ./fixtures/struts-orders right now so we can get moving.
evals.expected_output: No migration artifact files are generated. The response presents the Execution_Gate conditions (completed assessment or equivalent decision inputs, plus explicit strategy/target approval) and asks the user to choose between running the assessment or supplying the missing decision inputs.
expectations: Does not generate any migration artifact file (no Dockerfile, .dockerignore, or other execution-phase file is written)

Presents the Execution_Gate start conditions: a completed assessment or equivalent decision inputs (chosen Migration_Strategy and target compute model), plus explicit user approval of strategy and target path
Identifies which decision inputs are missing and offers exactly two options: run the modernization assessment, or provide the missing decision inputs
Does not treat the request itself as approval

evals.prompt: The assessment of ./fixtures/spring-boot-api is complete (Fit_Score 82, Rearchitect recommended). I approve: Rearchitect, target ECS on Fargate. Proceed with the migration — plan on containerizing, pushing to ECR, and standing up the environment.
evals.expected_output: On gate passage the skill presents the approved strategy, target path, and the list of planned action classes; before the first action of each class it obtains a separate confirmation presenting the concrete contents (output paths for file generation, ECR repository and tag for push, Terraform directory for apply), and executes nothing in a class before that class is confirmed.
expectations: Acknowledges the Execution_Gate passage by presenting the approved Migration_Strategy (Rearchitect), the target path (ECS on Fargate), and the list of planned action classes

Requests an individual confirmation per action class before its first execution — file generation (with output paths), image push (with ECR repository name and whether it must be created), terraform apply (with the target directory)
Does not execute any action belonging to a class whose per-class confirmation has not been given
Treats the strategy approval alone as insufficient to start pushing images or applying Terraform

evals.prompt: Gate passed: Replatform via .NET port approved for a solution with three net48 projects (Api.csproj, Web.csproj, Jobs.csproj), all targeting .NET 8. I confirmed AWS Transform is available in our account and our region. Build the transformation plan and tell me where AWS Transform helps.
evals.expected_output: A single ordered Transformation_Plan is presented before execution; Transform_Augmentation is proposed per work item within documented coverage with rationale along the four dimensions, same-type/same-rationale items are bundled into one proposal with per-item adoption, the '.NET agent-led porting has no public capability-difference evidence' statement appears, and no Transform job starts before adoption.
expectations: Constructs exactly one ordered Transformation_Plan and presents the work-item list and order to the user before starting any item

Proposes Transform_Augmentation only for work items whose transformation type is within AWS Transform's documented coverage, with rationale along the four dimensions: operational factors, local verifiability, scale, and transformation-type coverage
Bundles the three same-type items into a single proposal while keeping adoption identifiable per work item

Explicitly states that no public evidence of a capability difference between Transform augmentation and agent execution exists for .NET porting, guides the adoption decision on operational factors, and claims no superiority of either method without citable evidence
Does not start any AWS Transform job before the user adopts specific items

expectations: Grade the pre-execution commitment, not code execution: the graded deliverable is the ordered plan and the discipline the subject states it will follow before touching code — no code is expected to run in this eval, and its absence is not a deficiency
Presents the ordered Transformation_Plan (item list and order) before executing any item, and notes each item is agent-executed with the reason (AWS Transform unavailable per org policy)
States that all changes will be made only in the approved working branch migrate/java17 and never in the original source branch (any branch operations shown are confined to that branch)
Specifies a build verification (plus tests where available) and a checkpoint commit after each work item
States that a verification failure blocks subsequent items until it is resolved in the branch or the user chooses continue/skip/abort

Classifies the Web Site project and .ashx handler conversions as Agent_Executed_Items, each with the stated reason that the transformation type is outside AWS Transform's documented coverage
Proposes Transform_Augmentation only for the two supported class-library items
Reports the augmentation-applicability decision per work item (the two conditions: availability confirmed AND coverage)

evals.prompt: Migration execution for ./fixtures/spring-boot-api is at the environment step. Approved target: ECS on Fargate (Linux). Containerization done: image pushed as 123456789012.dkr.ecr.ap-northeast-1.amazonaws.com/spring-boot-api:v1, container listens on 8080, health endpoint /actuator/health, no local persistence detected, no session affinity needed. evals.prompt: terraform apply for the spring-boot-api environment just completed successfully and created two ECS services in cluster app-prod: 'web' (desired 2) and 'worker' (desired 2). Verify the deployment. Simulated AWS responses for your read-only calls: DescribeServices shows web running=2/desired=2 with the latest deployment COMPLETED; worker shows running=0/desired=2, latest deployment IN_PROGRESS, service events mention repeated task stops, and DescribeTasks on the stopped tasks returns stoppedReason 'CannotPullContainerError: pull access denied'.
evals.expected_output: Verification uses only Describe/List ECS read-only operations within the 10-minute / >=15-second-interval polling policy; web is reported steady, worker is reported not steady with a diagnosis from stopped-task reasons and service events; no AWS resources are created or modified without a new confirmation and overall success is not claimed.
expectations: Uses only ECS read-only operations whose names start with Describe or List for the verification, and reports which operations were used
Reports steady state per service, declaring it reached only where running count equals desired count and the latest deployment is completed — web reached, worker not reached
Honors the polling policy: checks at intervals of at least 15 seconds for at most 10 minutes from apply completion

For worker, reports the probable cause from the read-only evidence (stoppedReason CannotPullContainerError, service events) — e.g. an image pull/permission issue — and does not create or modify any AWS resource to fix it without a new user confirmation
Does not claim the deployment verification succeeded overall while worker has not reached steady state

Continues the confirmed action classes that do not depend on the refused class — generating the Containerization_Artifact (Dockerfile / .dockerignore) into ./migration-out; for this Linux Rearchitect/Fargate target the environment Terraform is delegated to ecs-build per the delegation boundary, not generated by this skill
Blocks the class that depends on the push artifact (applying the environment that references the image URI), explicitly stating the prerequisite artifact is missing
